newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Government held weekly meeting to discuss bill to ratify Romanian-Hungarian treaty, to analyse autumn farming campaign and preparations ahead of November 3 polls.
* Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu read report on recent CEFTA summit, with Romania due to start negotiations for joining the grouping.
* Parliament is expected to debate soon the bill to ratify Romanian-Hungarian treaty, foreign ministry spokesman Sorin Ducaru told the weekly news conference.
* He said Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu will sign the nuclear test ban treaty on September 24 at United Nations General Assembly meeting.

Melescanu would deliver speech at U.N. session on October 1, during debates on U.N. reform, Ducaru said. Melescanu is also expected to meet U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros Ghali and some of his western counterparts.

* In a reference to Moscow's critisism of Romania-Hungary treaty provision saying the two countries would support each other's bid to join NATO, Ducaru said that provision reflects the two countries' firm option to join the Western defence alliance and was not aimed against Russia.
* Ducaru said Romanians living abroad would be able to vote at polling stations in Romanian embassies. He said Romania would welcome international observers at November 3 polls.
* Some 12 million voters' cards are ready but only some 2.5 million have been mailed to Romania's voters, Adrian Duta, head of government's central elections department said.
Duta said distribution of voters' cards at polling stations on election day should be avoided.
* Ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) to launch its electoral programme this afternoon.
* National Unity Party (PUNR) leader Gheorghe Funar to register his candidacy for president later this afternoon.
* Lower Chamber of Deputies voted bill to allow state savings bank Casa de Economii si Consemnatiuni to give soft loans for housing construction.
Under the bill young families can get 20-year loans at 15 percent annual rate if they can pay 30 percent upfront. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
